title: What Is Execution?
excerpt: Execution is the ability to reach a set goal and complete a task.

inline.s: Execution is the ability to reach a set goal and complete a task.

In America there was a veteran who had been wounded on the battlefield. By the time he returned to civilian life, he was getting on in years, and with his wounds he had become a disabled veteran. Finding work had therefore become extremely difficult; many employers turned him away, yet each time he walked on with firm steps, continuing to seek out whatever opportunity he could find.

This time he came to one of the largest lumber companies in America to seek a job. He was turned away at the door by the hiring staff, who flatly refused to employ him. By one means and another he made his way through several checkpoints and at last found the company's vice president. He said to the vice president with great determination: "Vice President, as a veteran I solemnly promise you that I will complete any task you entrust to me. Please give me a chance." The vice president looked at his age and at his condition, and, as if in jest, did indeed give him a job.

What kind of job was it? It was a mess of a situation in the American Midwest. Before this, the company had sent many outstanding managers, and none had been able to do the job well, for there were dreadful client relations there, the company's outstanding debts had long gone uncollected, and the company's image there had been damaged. The vice president thought: since managers better than you could not complete this task, I might as well do you a favor and let you prove to yourself that you are not cut out for it. The veteran said: "I guarantee I will complete the task."

The next day he set off for that market, and a few months later he had restored the company's image there in the American Midwest, straightened out the client relations, and collected nearly all of the outstanding debts.

One weekend afternoon, the president called the veteran into his office and said: "I have to go out this weekend to take care of something. My sister is getting married in Utah, and I am going to attend her wedding. Please help me buy a gift: it is a blue vase in a very beautiful shop window of a certain gift shop." After describing it, he handed the veteran a card with the address written on it. Having received the task, the veteran solemnly promised his boss: "I guarantee I will complete the task!"

The veteran saw on the back of the card the number of the train car and seat in which his boss would be riding, for the boss had told him that once he had bought the vase, he need only deliver it to that car. So the veteran set out at once. He walked for a long time before he found the address, and when he found it, his mind went blank. For at that address there was simply no such shop as the boss had described, no beautiful shop window, and still less the blue vase.

Now, if it were you, what would you do? You might say to your boss: "I'm sorry, the address you gave me was wrong, so I had no way to buy the blue vase." But this veteran did not think that way, because he had promised his boss: I guarantee I will complete the task.

So his first thought was to call his boss to confirm, but his boss's phone would not go through. For on weekends in North America, a boss does not allow others to disturb him, and usually he does not answer his phone. What to do? Time passed minute by minute. Combining the map with a door-to-door sweep of the streets, at a spot five streets away from the address, the veteran at last saw the shop the boss had described. Looking at it from a distance — there was that beautiful shop window, and he could already see the blue vase. He was overjoyed, but when he dashed over, the door was already locked; the shop had closed early.

If it were you, what would you do? You would say: I'm sorry, boss, because the address you gave me was wrong, and after all my trouble to find the place, it had already closed. But this veteran did not think that way, because he had promised his boss: I guarantee I will complete the task. Combining the yellow pages and the address, the veteran at last found the phone number of the shop's manager. When he called to say he wanted to buy the blue vase, the other party said: "I'm on vacation; the shop is closed." And then hung up.

If it were you, you would say: I'm sorry, boss, the shop is closed, so I couldn't buy it. You would find a whole pile of reasons to explain why you had not completed the task. But this veteran did not think that way, because he had promised his boss: I guarantee I will complete the task. He was thinking that even if he had to pay a heavy price, he must obtain the blue vase. He thought of smashing the shop window to get the blue vase, and so the veteran turned to go and find a tool. When he had, after much trouble, found a tool and returned, a policeman happened to arrive from afar, fully armed. The policeman came up before the shop window and stood there, motionless. Then the veteran waited patiently; he waited a long while, but the policeman showed not the slightest sign of leaving.

At this moment the veteran realized something, and he once again dialed the manager's phone number. His first words were: I stake my life and the honor of a soldier that I must obtain that blue vase, because I have made a promise, and this bears on a soldier's honor and life. Please help me. The man no longer hung up, and kept listening to him. He recounted how he had been wounded on the battlefield, how on the battlefield he had promised his comrade that he would save his comrade's life, that he would carry his comrade out of the battlefield, and that for this he had been gravely wounded and left disabled. The manager was moved, and at last agreed to send someone to open the shop door and sell him the blue vase.

The veteran got the blue vase and was very happy. But then he looked at the time: his boss's train had already left. If it were you, what would you do? You would find a pile of reasons to explain to your boss: the address you gave me was wrong; after much trouble I found the place, but it had closed; I met with setbacks and endured hardships, and finally got the blue vase, but your train had already left. But this veteran did not think that way, because he had promised his boss: I guarantee I will complete the task. So the veteran called a former comrade; he wanted to charter a private plane. Because in North America many people own private planes, he at last found someone willing to rent him one, and then he flew in pursuit of the next station of his boss's train. When he ran panting onto the platform, his boss's train was just slowly pulling in.

He walked to his boss's car according to the car number the boss had told him, and saw the boss sitting there quietly. He placed the blue vase carefully on the table and said to his boss: "President, here is the blue vase you wanted. Please give my regards to your sister, and I wish you a pleasant journey." Then he turned and got off the train.

When the new week began, on the first day of work, the boss called the veteran into his office and said: "Thank you for buying the gift; my sister liked it very much. You completed the task, and I thank you. In fact, for several years now the company has been choosing a manager to send to the Far East as president. It is the company's most important department, but in the process of selecting a manager we had never been able to find one to our satisfaction. Later, a consulting firm devised a 'blue vase test' as the method of selecting the manager. In the course of the selection, most people did not complete the task. This was because the address we gave was false, we had the shop manager close early, and we allowed him to answer only two calls. In the past tests, only one person completed the task — and that was because he smashed the shop window glass and got the blue vase. We felt that this did not accord with our company's code of ethics, and so we did not hire him."

And so, in the later tests, we specially hired a fully armed policeman to stand guard there. But none of this stood in the way of your determination to complete the task. You completed the task brilliantly. Now, on behalf of the board of directors, I formally appoint you president of our company's Far East division.... What is execution? This is execution!
